title: Basic Prepositions for Place and Time
goal: Choose basic Norwegian prepositions for simple places, movement, visits, future time, past time, and duration.

objectives.statement: Choose basic Norwegian prepositions for simple places, movement, visits, future time, past time, and duration.

prompt.value: Write a connected practical message from Emil. Say that he is currently at work, will leave in half an hour, will travel to Bergen, and will stay with his sister Lea for two days. Also say that he will be at Lea’s place and that Lea travelled to Oslo one week ago. Use suitable forms from i, på, hos, til, om, for … siden, and durational i.

payload.judge_prompt: Check only whether the connected message communicates the requested situation using appropriate Norwegian place and time prepositions. Report evidence for every criterion. Treat reasonable changes in sentence order and supporting verb forms as acceptable.

criteria.instruction: States that Emil is currently at work using the conventional current-location phrase **på jobb**.
States that Emil will travel to Bergen using **til Bergen** for the destination.
States that Emil will be at Lea’s place using **hos Lea**.
States that Emil will leave in half an hour using **om en halvtime**.
States that Lea travelled to Oslo one week ago using the frame **for en uke siden**.
States that Emil’s stay with Lea lasts two days using durational **i to dager**.

prompt.value: Write six fresh, short Norwegian examples in your own words: one for current location, one for a destination, one for a visit location, one for future time from now, one for past time before now, and one for activity duration. Keep every example in Norwegian and make each meaning clear from its context.

payload.judge_prompt: Check for six distinct Norwegian examples with the requested meanings. Accept any natural, simple example grounded in the taught patterns. Report evidence for every criterion; do not require specific people, places, or time quantities.

criteria.instruction: Gives a natural current-location example using taught **i** or **på** usage and a clear Norwegian context.
Gives a destination example using **til** and makes the destination meaning clear from the Norwegian context.
Gives a visit-location example using **hos** with a person or professional and a clear Norwegian context.
Gives a future-time-from-now example using **om** plus an amount of time and a clear Norwegian context.
Gives a past-time-before-now example using **for … siden** with the amount inside the frame and a clear Norwegian context.
Gives an activity-duration example using **i** plus an amount of time and a clear Norwegian context.
